edits.location: How to get a prenup: Step 5
edits.issue: fact_12 (Legal Aid NSW) says you don't go to court to make one and it is enforceable once made; 'From there' ties enforceability to signing alone, drifting past the formal requirements, and the claim is uncredited
edits.old: From there it is legally enforceable without any court step. <!-- fact_12 -->
edits.new: Legal Aid NSW notes you don't go to court to make one, but once made it is legally enforceable. <!-- fact_12 -->

fact_check_log.claim: Prenup is a financial agreement under Part VIIIA / Div 4 Part VIIIAB (FCFCOA)
Binding agreement ousts Court jurisdiction; can contract out of proceedings (FCFCOA)
Can cover the field or only some issues (FCFCOA)
Before/during/after marriage, ss 90B, 90C, 90D (FCFCOA)
De facto ss 90UB, 90UC, 90UD (FCFCOA)
Binding only if s 90G / s 90UJ technical requirements met (FCFCOA)
Mandatory independent legal advice from Australian legal practitioner (FCFCOA)
Court may set aside, s 90K / s 90UM (FCFCOA)
Law described as very complex (FCFCOA)
Cannot enter without independent advice from Australian lawyer (FCFCOA Separate smarter)
BFA definition, division on separation, spousal and child maintenance (Legal Aid NSW)
Three types; no court to make one; once made legally enforceable (Legal Aid NSW)

Step 5: 'From there it is legally enforceable without any court step' implies enforceability follows signing alone; source says no court to make it, enforceable once made, and validity depends on all formal requirements. Fixed by edit.
Eight formal requirements (Legal Aid NSW)
Usually cannot go to court later; stays in force on death; set aside only in limited circumstances (Legal Aid NSW)
Set-aside grounds incl. fraud, unconscionable conduct (Legal Aid NSW)
Overseas agreement not automatically recognised; must meet formal requirements; property settlement orders possible (Legal Aid NSW)
Written, no court approval, own lawyers, both sign, lawyer's signed statement (Victoria Legal Aid)
Property division and ongoing spousal maintenance (Victoria Legal Aid)
Unfair conduct, formal requirements not followed, not followed, government seizure (Victoria Legal Aid)
Change or end by new agreement / termination agreement / abandonment (Victoria Legal Aid, Legal Aid NSW)
Protect inheritance, children's property, reduce disputes, one document (Legal Aid NSW)
Assets to protect such as property or super; also known as a prenup (Moneysmart)
Both sign and seek legal and financial advice (Moneysmart)
Act headings for ss 90G, 90H, 90J (legislation.gov.au)
Bankruptcy trustee and bankruptcy limits (Legal Aid NSW)
